analysis.title: The 720: 2027 Global Outlooks - Macro, Markets, Strategy, & Commodities; China 2027 Macro Outlook, NVDA, SMIC
key_insights: Global Macro Outlook 2027 (Hatzius): global GDP growth of 2.8% in 2027 as lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions. Risks skew to the downside from a renewed energy shock, bond market turbulence and a weaker AI impulse.
Core inflation slows in 2027 as US tariff pass-through ends, with US core PCE forecast to fall to 2.4% from 3.2%.

Policy path: two more Fed hikes and one ECB hike, then both central banks return to cuts in late 2027. GS policy rate forecasts are generally below market pricing, so longer-term rates are expected to come down modestly.
Asset allocation: overweight the US and Japan, underweight Europe. Bonds are regaining hedging value as downside growth risks rise, and credit spreads will likely widen.

Global Markets Outlook (Trivedi, Wilson): the macro baseline is friendly (stable growth, declining inflation) but an aging market cycle faces risks from higher real rates and wider credit spreads. The AI investment impulse as a share of GDP is forecast to peak in early 2027.
S&P 500 earnings growth is forecast to slow to 11% in 2027 from 36% in 2026. GS recommends diversified allocations given a more two-sided risk picture.

US 10-year Treasury yield forecast is 4.6% by end-2027. The broad trade-weighted Dollar is forecast to decline in 2027, especially against Asia's revaluing currencies such as the Yen and Yuan. EM assets are highlighted for high, diversified yields and a regionally diversified earnings mix.

Global Equity Strategy (Oppenheimer): positive but highly volatile global equity returns in 2027. Overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, underweight Europe. The equity bull market is expected to continue as valuations de-rate and inflation, bond yields and oil ease.

Equity positioning: balance long-duration Growth with selective Defensives and rate-sensitive sectors. Attractive entry points in US Hyperscalers on balance sheet strength, and US Healthcare is favored as a beneficiary of lower bond yields.

Commodity Views (Struyven, Dart): positive commodities allocation for tactical and structural hedging, with geopolitical risk premia having fallen sharply. Base case 2027 average Brent $88/bbl and TTF 45EUR/MWh. Brent is forecast to fall to $78/bbl by end-2027 from around $100/bbl.

Commodity trades: long summer 2027 European gasoline and 27Q1 TTF call spreads for asymmetric upside against winter weather or Middle East supply shocks. Reiterates long December 2027 copper, short aluminum, with copper forecast at $15,600/t on AI and electrification demand against constrained mine supply.
Gold: December 2027 forecast lowered to $4,650/toz on a more hawkish Fed rate outlook, while GS stays constructive longer term on central bank buying.

China Macro 2027 Outlook (Hui Shan): real GDP growth moderates to 4.5% in 2027 from 4.6% in 2026, slightly above consensus, helped by roughly 1ppt less drag from property and fiscal tightening. Uncertainty rises ahead of the 21st Party Congress in 2H27 and with potentially less stable US-China relations.

China: headline CPI forecast at 0.5% in 2027, significantly below consensus. Current account surplus rises to 4.9% of GDP. A 10bps policy rate cut is expected in 4Q27, taking the overnight OMO rate to 1.15%. Long-end yields trend lower, CNY appreciates gradually, and GS stays Overweight China equities with mid-to-high teen returns expected into 2027.

Nvidia: CEO Jensen Huang resigned and CFO Colette Kress becomes Interim CEO. GS cuts its 12m TP to $220 from $300 on limited visibility, the transition and execution risk, but keeps Buy. GS calls it a meaningful but measured negative and flags a US DOJ investigation into potential export control violations.

Nvidia: GS argues Huang's absence could make negotiating new multi-party ecosystem investments harder and sees heightened execution risk over 12-18 months, though execution on the next two product generations is well underway. Direct financial impact is expected to be measured given the long-dated backlog. GS CY27 EPS estimate is $16.70 versus Street consensus of $15.91.

SMIC 3Q26: operating profit 31% above consensus on higher wafer shipments and a 29.9% gross margin (4.0ppt above consensus). 4Q26 revenue guided up 4-6% QoQ with gross margin easing to 26-28%. GS raises 2026E-29E net income estimates 8-9% and revenue estimates 1-10%, citing generative AI demand in China and localization.
Recruit 2Q: Indeed's higher unit prices reflect sustainable monetization, with AI-driven productivity supporting the unchanged 50% medium-term margin target.

Sumitomo Electric 1H: optical device output expected stable in 2H, data center server purchase value growth outlook raised to a 47% CAGR for FY26-FY30, optical device production to rise 7X from FY25 to FY30, optical connector capacity 21X from FY25 to FY29, with full CPO ramp around 2028.

Pan Pacific International 1Q27: operating profit of 44.1bn yen up 7% YoY, slightly above guidance, with discount store profit up only 1% on growth investments. Full-year guidance maintained and Toys R Us expected to book a 3bn yen operating loss in FY27.

Rohto 2Q27: operating profit missed GS and LSEG consensus on lower US eye drop shipments after an FDA-related suspension at the Vietnam plant. Full-year guidance maintained on expected Japan and Asia upside.

Samsung F&M 3Q26: net profit in line with lowered consensus, a 23% YoY fall in investment profit offset by 6.9% insurance profit growth. Acquiring a further 40.6% of Canopius for US$1.67bn, guided to add 1ppt of ROE. GS expects investor focus to shift to excess capital returns.

Hindustan Aeronautics 2QFY27: PAT 4% above consensus and revenue up 15% YoY beating consensus by 2%, but EBITDA missed GS by 8% on lower gross margins. GS sees it as the most attractive name in India Defense and Aerospace coverage.

Montage management meeting: AI inferencing and agentic AI lift server CPU shipments and memory channel counts, supporting RCD chip demand through DDR5 generation migration. Second-generation MRDIMM products are ready for mass production.

China Restaurants October update: demand remained choppy and no clear 4Q26 inflection has appeared. Haidilao table turns fell mid-single-digits YoY, drinks held up, Chagee beat GS expectations and announced a special dividend implying about a 16% yield. GS cut Juewei 2026-28E net profit estimates 9-22% after a 3Q26 EBIT miss.

Americas Investment Banks: after a median 6% 3Q26 sector earnings beat, top-line growth should continue on large-cap strategic M&A and restructuring. The group is back to mid-cycle and fairly valued, so limited multiple rerating is expected. Top picks are EVR, LCLN, PIPR and PJT.

SEMICON Europa takeaways: semiconductor equipment demand is very strong with no deceleration in orders. VAT Group customer planning windows now extend three quarters ahead, and Ebara expects to deliver 5,500 vacuum pumps next year on a backlog almost twice normal. Competition is rising in Chinese sub-fab equipment.

tension_points.bear_case: Downside growth risks from a renewed energy shock, bond market turbulence and a weaker AI impulse, plus higher real rates and wider credit spreads late in an aging cycle.
